<!-- Generated from libs/server/config/src/lib/registry by its tests. Do not edit by hand: change the registry and run `pnpm nx test server-config -- -u`. -->

QAuth reads its configuration from environment variables. This page lists every QAuth key the auth server and the developer portal read, generated from the configuration key registry in `libs/server/config/src/lib/registry/`. A test fails when the page, the registry and the env schemas disagree. Variables of the Node.js runtime itself, such as `UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE`, are not listed.

## Stability tiers

Every key has a tier, which says how it may change ([ADR-018 §5](/reference/records/adr/018-1-0-scope-and-stability/)).

- **Stable** keys follow the deprecation policy. A deprecation is announced in a minor release; the old name or behaviour keeps working, with a warning at boot, for at least 12 months, and it is removed only in a new major release.
- **Advanced** keys may change in a minor release. Read the release notes before you upgrade a deployment that sets one.
- **Experimental** keys may change at any time, without a deprecation window. The server logs a warning at boot for each experimental key that is set, and for each key set to an experimental value. A key or value that switches on an [experimental feature](/reference/experimental-features/) warns through that feature instead, once the feature is on.

## Roles

Every key has a role, which says who owns its value ([ADR-019 Decision 10](/reference/records/adr/019-deployment-topology-and-trust-boundaries/)).

- **deployment**: the environment owns the value, for the whole deployment.
- **realm-seed**: a realm policy, which the realm row owns. The key seeds a new realm, and a realm that had no policies at its first boot after the upgrade that put them on the row; a later change of the key changes no existing realm. Until the server reads the policy from the realm row, it still applies the key to every realm, unless its description says it reads the realm row. The Role column names the policy the key seeds.

A key marked **Secret** holds a credential. This page never shows its value, not even as a default, and neither does the boot log.

## Stable keys

### Server

| Key                 | Role       | Default                                                                   | Since | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------- | ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ADMIN_API_ENABLED` | deployment | `false`                                                                   | 0.2.0 | Run the admin API on its own internal listener, on a process whose `SERVICE_ROLES` holds `admin`, off by default until the first admin operations (#517) and DPoP-bound admin tokens (#520) ship; `false` serves no admin API on this process, and the public listener never serves it.                                                                                                                           |
| `ADMIN_API_HOST`    | deployment | `127.0.0.1`                                                               | 0.2.0 | The address the admin API's listener binds to, loopback by default, and loopback only in production until admin tokens are DPoP-bound (#520); the listener grants nothing for a caller's network position, so every call but the one for its OpenAPI document needs an admin token.                                                                                                                               |
| `ADMIN_API_PORT`    | deployment | `3002`                                                                    | 0.2.0 | The TCP port the admin API's listener binds to; it must differ from `PORT`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `CORS_ORIGIN`       | deployment | none in `production`, so cross-origin requests are refused; `*` otherwise | 0.1.0 | The origins, comma-separated, allowed to call the server cross-origin.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `ENABLE_SWAGGER`    | deployment | `true`, or `false` when `NODE_ENV=production`                             | 0.1.0 | Serve the Swagger UI at `/docs`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `HOST`              | deployment | `0.0.0.0`                                                                 | 0.1.0 | The address the auth server listens on.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `NODE_ENV`          | deployment | `development`                                                             | 0.1.0 | The runtime mode, `development`, `test` or `production`; `production` turns on the strict boot checks, such as refusing the development session secret.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `PORT`              | deployment | `3000`                                                                    | 0.1.0 | The TCP port the auth server listens on.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `SERVICE_ROLES`     | deployment | `all`                                                                     | 0.2.0 | The roles this process runs, `all` or a comma-separated list of `web` (the browser-session endpoints), `api` (the token, discovery, account and developer endpoints), `admin`, `signer` (the KEK and every private key) and `delivery` (event delivery); each role registers only its own routes, plugins and jobs, and a process without `signer` refuses to boot when it finds a KEK or a private key variable. |
| `TRUST_PROXY`       | deployment | `false`                                                                   | 0.1.0 | The reverse proxies whose `X-Forwarded-For` hops set the client address and whose `X-Forwarded-Host` names the realm host, as a comma-separated list of addresses, CIDR ranges or `loopback`, `linklocal` and `uniquelocal`; `true` and a hop count are refused.                                                                                                                                                  |

## Experimental keys

No key is experimental.

### Experimental values

These values of stable and advanced keys are experimental, and the server warns at boot when one is set. A value that switches on an [experimental feature](/reference/experimental-features/) warns through that feature instead, once the feature is on.

| Key                       | Experimental values |
| ------------------------- | ------------------- |
| `OID4VP_VERIFIER_PROFILE` | `oid4vp-1.0-base`   |

## Renamed keys

A renamed key keeps working under its old name for the deprecation window.

- Only the old name is set: the server uses its value and logs a warning at boot.
- Both names are set to the same value: the server logs a warning at boot.
- Both names are set to different values: the server refuses to start, and the error names both.

| Old name                 | Use instead                | Deprecated since |
| ------------------------ | -------------------------- | ---------------- |
| `REQUIRE_EMAIL_VERIFIED` | `REQUIRE_VERIFIED_ACCOUNT` | 0.1.0            |

## Removed keys

The server no longer reads these keys and refuses to start while one is set, whatever its value. The error names the key and what replaces it.

| Key                              | Removed in | Instead                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| -------------------------------- | ---------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `CIMD_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ADDRESSES`   | 0.2.0      | A metadata document or client jwks_uri never reaches a private address now; list an operator-set private destination in the file EGRESS_ALLOWLIST_PATH names, and reach a test server through createTestEgressClient.                                           |
| `ID_JAG_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ADDRESSES` | 0.2.0      | A trusted issuer's discovery URL on a private address is listed, for its realms, in the file EGRESS_ALLOWLIST_PATH names; the jwks_uri its discovery document names never reaches a private address. Tests reach a local issuer through createTestEgressClient. |

## Adding a key

A pull request that adds, renames or removes a key registers the change in the same pull request: an entry in `libs/server/config/src/lib/registry/keys/`, with its tier, role, default and one sentence, and a regenerated page; a removed key moves to `registry/removed.ts`. A stable key also appears in `.env.example`. A test fails until all three agree.
